Tenant.title: Tenant
Tenant.description: Represents a single business or store instance within the FreshTally multi-tenant application, holding core settings and identifying data ownership.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Tenant entity.

name.description: The legal or common name of the business/store.

currency.description: The primary currency used for transactions and reporting (e.g., 'USD', 'EUR').

taxRate.description: The default tax rate applied to sales, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.05 for 5%).

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the tenant record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the tenant record was last updated.

UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Stores user-specific data, including their role and association with a tenant, for access control and personalization.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity. This typically corresponds to an external authentication system's user ID.

tenantId.description: Reference to the Tenant this user belongs to. (Relationship: Tenant 1:N UserProfile)

email.description: The user's email address, used for identification and communication.

role.description: The user's role within the tenant (e.g., 'owner', 'staff') defining their access permissions.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user profile was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the user profile was last updated.

Product.title: Product
Product.description: Details about a product available for sale or managed in inventory, including pricing and stock levels.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Product entity.

tenantId.description: Reference to the Tenant that owns this product. (Relationship: Tenant 1:N Product)

description.description: A detailed description of the product.

price.description: The current selling price of the product.

cost.description: The cost of the product to the business, used for profit calculation.

stockLevel.description: The current quantity of the product in stock.

sku.description: Stock Keeping Unit, a unique identifier for the product often used for inventory tracking.

isActive.description: Indicates if the product is currently available for sale or active in inventory.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the product record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the product record was last updated.

Transaction.title: Transaction
Transaction.description: Represents a single point-of-sale transaction, capturing overall details of a customer purchase.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Transaction entity.

tenantId.description: Reference to the Tenant where this transaction occurred. (Relationship: Tenant 1:N Transaction)

transactionDate.description: The date and time when the transaction was completed.

totalAmount.description: The total monetary amount of the transaction, including tax and discounts.

paymentMethod.description: The method used by the customer to pay (e.g., 'cash', 'card', 'mobile_pay').

status.description: The current status of the transaction (e.g., 'completed', 'pending', 'cancelled').

cashierId.description: Reference to the UserProfile of the staff member who processed the transaction. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Transaction)

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the transaction record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the transaction record was last updated.

TransactionItem.title: TransactionItem
TransactionItem.description: Represents a single line item within a transaction, detailing a specific product or custom item sold.

id.description: Unique identifier for the TransactionItem entity.

tenantId.description: Reference to the Tenant where this transaction item belongs. (Relationship: Tenant 1:N TransactionItem)

transactionId.description: Reference to the Transaction this item is part of. (Relationship: Transaction 1:N TransactionItem)

productId.description: Reference to the Product sold, if it's an existing product. Can be null for custom items. (Relationship: Product 1:N TransactionItem)

productName.description: The name of the product or custom item sold. A snapshot of the product name or a custom entry.

quantity.description: The quantity of the item sold.

unitPrice.description: The unit price of the item at the time of sale. A snapshot of the product price.

subtotal.description: The total price for this line item (quantity * unitPrice).

isCustomItem.description: Indicates if this is a custom product entry not linked to an existing Product record.

Expense.title: Expense
Expense.description: Records a business expenditure, categorized for financial tracking and reporting.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Expense entity.

tenantId.description: Reference to the Tenant incurring this expense. (Relationship: Tenant 1:N Expense)

description.description: A brief description of the expense.

amount.description: The monetary amount of the expense.

expenseDate.description: The date when the expense was incurred.

category.description: The category of the expense, often determined by an AI categorization tool (e.g., 'Supplies', 'Rent', 'Utilities', 'Marketing').

receiptUrl.description: Optional URL to a digital image or document of the receipt.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the expense record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the expense record was last updated.

firestore.reasoning:
The recommended Firestore structure for FreshTally is designed with a strong emphasis on multi-tenancy, strict authorization independence, and simplified security rules. All core operational data is rooted under a `/tenants/{tenantId}` collection, ensuring natural data segregation for each business instance. User-specific profiles, containing the crucial 'tenantId' and 'role' fields, are stored in a top-level `/userProfiles/{userId}` collection. This design adheres to the core principles as follows:

**Authorization Independence:** Every document (except the root `Tenant` itself, which is implicitly identified by its path) within the tenant-scoped collections (e.g., `products`, `transactions`, `expenses`, `transactionItems`) explicitly contains a `tenantId` field. The `UserProfile` also stores its `tenantId` and `role`. This denormalization is critical: it means that security rules do not need to perform `get()` operations on parent documents to determine ownership or scope for each read/write request on tenant data. Instead, rules can perform a *single* `get()` on the authenticated user's `UserProfile` document (`/userProfiles/$(request.auth.uid)`) to ascertain their associated `tenantId` and `role`. Subsequently, for any tenant-scoped data, the rule simply compares the `resource.data.tenantId` with the `tenantId` retrieved from the user's profile, eliminating complex and costly recursive lookups.

**QAPs (Queries are not Filters):** This structure inherently supports Query-As-Predicate (QAP). All tenant-specific data is accessed via paths that include the `{tenantId}` wildcard (e.g., `/tenants/{tenantId}/products`). Security rules will be configured to match the `tenantId` in the request path (and in the document's data) against the `tenantId` of the authenticated user (obtained from their `UserProfile`). This strong path-based authorization, coupled with the explicit `tenantId` in every document, means that `list` operations are automatically constrained. A user can only successfully query within *their* tenant's path, and the rules will prevent any attempt to list data across different tenants or for a tenant they don't belong to, without requiring additional database filters or post-query processing. The homogeneous security posture within each tenant-scoped collection (Strategy B) further simplifies this, as all documents within, for example, `/tenants/{tenantId}/products`, share the same `tenantId` and therefore the same primary access requirements.

**Hierarchical Access and Nested Data:** The use of hierarchical paths for tenant-owned data (e.g., `/tenants/{tenantId}/products`) and further nesting for related entities (e.g., `/tenants/{tenantId}/transactions/{transactionId}/transactionItems`) provides clear ownership and logical grouping. This continues the `1:N` relationship pattern for data organization, making rule writing intuitive and data exploration predictable.
